newsitem.title: USA: Dow snaps record streak, temp staffing shares hit.
newsitem.headline: Dow snaps record streak, temp staffing shares hit.

text.p: U.S. stocks pulled back from record heights on modest profit-taking on Thursday, with temporary employment shares hammered by an earnings warning from Olsten Corp.

"After the feeding frenzy of the past couple of weeks, investors are taking a bit of a breather here. There's a bit of profit-taking, nothing dramatic," said Charlie Crane, director of research at Spears Benzak Salomon and Farrell.
After setting November's 10th record closing high on Wednesday, the Dow industrials slipped 12 to about 6418.
The Nasdaq Composite lost seven to about 1258 as heavyweights Intel and Microsoft gave up some of their recent strong gains. Intel lost two to 118-7/8 and Microsoft was off 2-7/8 to 150-3/8.
Winners and losers were even on very heavy NYSE volume of about 468 million shares.

"It looks like we're making a bit of a pitstop. Some profit-taking has kicked in but by and large the tilt appears to be up. There appears to be some nervousness about the market's big move over the past 10 days," said Alan Ackerman, a market strategist at Fahnestock and Co.
Attention focused on the temporary staffing sector. "That's all related to Olsten," said Hildegard Zagorski, a Prudential Securities market analyst.

Olsten was the most-active NYSE issue and shed 28 percent or 5-1/2 points to 14-3/8 after forecasting fourth quarter earnings will fall far below expectations. It cited ongoing margin pressures affecting its two primary businesses and lower revenues from Medicare operations. Prudential cut Olsten.
Among others in the group, Accustaff lost 2-3/8 to 21-1/8, Interim Services lost 3-1/8 to 36, Robert Half lost 2-3/8 to 35-7/8, Norrell fell 1-3/8 to 22-7/8 and Manpower fell 3/4 to 31-1/8.

The long bond lost 5/32 to yield 6.42 percent as a large issuance of fresh corporate supply weighed on prices. Bonds had surged after news that weekly jobless claims rose to a stronger-than-expected 344,000.

After the closing bell, Applied Materials reported sharply lower fourth-quarter earnings. The leading maker of water fabrication systems for the semiconductor industry also forecast the industry downturn extending through early 1997. The stock ended up 1-1/2 to 32. "This might pressure the chip stocks tomorrow, specifically the commodity chip makers," said Phil Orlando of Value Line Asset Management.
In after-hours trading, Applied Materials fell 1-1/8.

Among other issues, Texaco lost one to 98-7/8. The city of Philadelphia's pension board voted to divest $5.5 million worth of Texaco stock, citing evidence of racial bias. It referred to secretly taped recordings of Texaco executives laced with racial slurs.

Conrail lost 2-1/4 to 94-5/8. CSX Corp said its $110 cash tender offer for shares of Conrail was oversubscribed. CSX proceeded with its offer after a federal appeals court on Wednesday denied Norfolk Southern's effort to block it. CSX lost one to 45-5/8 and Norfolk Southern fell 1/2 to 87-1/2.
Guidant surged 3-1/4 to 53-1/2 after news the stock will be added to the S&P 500 index to replace Bally Entertainment which is being acquired by Hilton Hotels.
Panavision, a designer and maker of high-precision film camera systems, climbed three to 20 in its Wall Street debut.
Zebra Technologies lost 4-1/2 to 25-1/2 and Eltron International shed 5-7/8 to 32-3/8 after news that they had ended merger talks because of concerns over who would control the combined company.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 6.86 to 1258.08.
The S&P 500 index fell 1.20 to 742.75.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721.
